items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: We were met by the manager of the Taj Mahal Hotel who was a Mr. Faletti... and two Negro musicians who were living in India and were going to play with the Abbey band. One was Cricket Smith, a trumpet player and the other was Rudy Jackson, an alto sax man.

ctx.x: We met an American white couple who were dancers that were also going to Bombay to work at the Taj Mahal. They were known as Tracey and Hay. The fellow was Sid Tracey and the woman was Bessie Hay. The 28th of October we arrived in Aden, Arabia and went ashore with Hay and Tracey. We took photographs posing with camels that didn't have a life that was easy like those in the zoos. These camels had to work. We posed with shark teeth and with the natives. We had stopped the day before at Massawa which was Italian…

The whole voyage was wonderful and I felt as though I was living in wonderland. We arrived at Bombay the 2nd of November, ten sailing days from Venice. We were met by the manager of the Taj Mahal Hotel who was a Mr. Faletti, an Italian who was a naturalised English citizen, and two Negro musicians who were living in India and were going to play with the Abbey band. One was Cricket Smith, a trumpet player and the other was Rudy Jackson, an alto sax man. Cricket and Rudy had come to Europe in the early 20s.

We has seen many exciting things in the port towns we visited but Bombay gassed them all. The taxis were opened top five passenger cars, mostly American made, and I could see in front, on the sides and from the back without any difficulties. There were so many sights to see that I almost had a sore neck turning it so much from the time we left the port until we reached the Taj Mahal Hotel. One sees different events in newsreels and also movies about India which are very interesting but when you see these things…
